title: Power Platform: create and manage Dataverse filter-based security filters in the Power Apps maker portal
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap dates, preview behaviour, licensing background and automation are supported. The maker paths stop on the correct forms but should identify their deciding fields, and the user-role control should clarify that it manages direct assignments only.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Microsoft plans a simplified maker-portal experience for admins and makers to create and manage filter-based security filters.
claims.quote: Admins and makers can create and manage filters for Filter-based Security through a simplified management experience.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes centralised filter management for record access without individually sharing records.
claims.quote: policy-driven record access without individually sharing records. ... Organizations can more easily configure and maintain Filter-based Security policies through a centralized experience.

claims.claim: Filter-based security grants Dataverse record access through matching data conditions rather than record ownership.
claims.quote: Ownership-based security grants access through record ownership, teams, business units, and organization-level privileges. Filter-based security grants access through record data that satisfies filter criteria.

claims.claim: A filter can grant access to accounts whose City is Redmond.
claims.quote: For example, an organization wants users to access only accounts located in Redmond. Configure the filter on the account table and add a condition where the City column equals Redmond.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; controls[0].note; controls[1].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The underlying filter-based security feature and its documented configuration are in preview.
claims.quote: This feature is in preview. Preview features aren't meant for production use and may have restricted functionality.

claims.claim: A Record Filter stores the FetchXML definition selecting accessible records.
claims.quote: Record Filter: Uses FetchXML to identify records that qualify for access.

claims.claim: FetchXML is Dataverse's XML query language.
claims.quote: FetchXML is a proprietary XML-based query language used to retrieve data from Dataverse.

claims.claim: An Entity Record Filter associates a Record Filter with a Dataverse table.
claims.quote: Entity Record Filter: Associates a Record Filter with a Dataverse table.

claims.claim: Associating a Record Filter with a table creates filter privileges.
claims.quote: When you associate a Record Filter with a table through an Entity Record Filter, Dataverse creates filter privileges.

claims.claim: Filter privileges support Create, Read, Write, Delete, Append and Append To operations.
claims.quote: Filter privileges support these data access operations: Create. Read. Write. Delete. Append. Append To.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Governance controls; summary
claims.claim: An administrator grants filter privileges through security roles.
claims.quote: All activated entity record filter security predicates for a table can be granted by an admin to a security role. Roles can be assigned to the Create, Read, Write, Delete, Append and Append to privileges.

claims.claim: The current Learn procedure builds filter conditions using a model-driven app's filter editor.
claims.quote: Open your model-driven app for editing. Open a table where you want to create filtered view record ownership, such as Accounts. Select Filters on the top right-hand corner of the action bar.

claims.claim: The current Learn procedure downloads the filter as FetchXML.
claims.quote: Select Download FetchXML when you're done with selecting all the fields and operators.

claims.claim: The downloaded FetchXML is pasted into a Record Filter created from a solution.
claims.quote: Go to Solutions and create a new solution or open an existing solution. Select + New. Select More and Other. Select Record Filter. ... Copy the FetchXML and paste it in the FetchXML box.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether the new screen appears automatically or requires an administrator to enable it.
claims.quote: Searched: 'filter-based security maker portal enable default licensing pricing'; 'Create and manage Filter-based Maker portal'. Read roadmap and Learn's Filter-based security, Filtered record ownership and developer configuration pages; none states the new screen's arrival default.

claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe the new simplified maker-portal screen; the listed paths are the existing documented configuration.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Create and manage Filter-based Maker portal'; 'filter-based security maker portal enable default licensing pricing'. Opened Filter-based security and Filtered record ownership, including the code article; results describe current solution-based configuration, not the new screen.

claims.claim: No source states that existing roles or filters change when the new screen ships.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Create and manage Filter-based Maker portal'; 'filter-based security maker portal enable default licensing pricing'. Read roadmap and Filter-based security, Filtered record ownership and developer configuration pages; no migration or automatic modification is described.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Editing a filter already granted by a role can change access for that role's holders without changing the role itself.
claims.quote: A record filter contains a FetchXML query that defines which rows a user can access. ... Before changing or removing a filter, review every role that grants it to avoid unintended changes in data access.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises reviewing every role granting a filter before changing or removing it.
claims.quote: Before changing or removing a filter, review every role that grants it to avoid unintended changes in data access.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout; rationale: risk
claims.claim: On user/team-owned tables, filter privileges supplement existing access and do not reduce broader access.
claims.quote: For user or team record ownership tables, filter privileges add row-level access to ownership-based security. They don't replace or reduce access granted through ownership, sharing, or security role privileges.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Supplemental filter access can include records across business unit boundaries.
claims.quote: Filtered view permissions supplement these existing access mechanisms by granting additional access to records that match configured filter conditions, including records across business unit boundaries, without changing the table's ownership type.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no approval step for filter edits.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Dataverse Record Filter editing approval privileges auditing filter security maker portal'; 'record filter approval Dataverse'. Read developer Manage filter records and Record Filter table Messages; standard updates and role review are documented, but no approval step.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Creating a filtered-ownership table creates an All records filter privilege and grants it to the System Administrator role.
claims.quote: When you create a filtered record ownership table, Dataverse creates a global All records filter privilege and grants it to the System Administrator security role.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: System Administrators can see all rows of filtered-ownership tables through the All records permission.
claims.quote: A Power Platform admin can see all records because the admin has global All records permission on the Read privilege.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises testing filters with a non-administrator account because administrators receive All records access.
claims.quote: Test with a nonadministrator account because system administrators receive the All records filter and don't experience the same row restrictions.

claims.claim: The filtered record ownership Learn prerequisites require System Administrator to create the security roles required for the feature.
claims.quote: To create and assign the security roles required for this feature you need the system administrator security role.

claims.claim: The filtered record ownership Learn prerequisites require System Administrator to assign the roles required for this feature.
claims.quote: To create and assign the security roles required for this feature you need the system administrator security role.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Change & support
claims.claim: Dataverse applies filter permissions on every query.
claims.quote: Does filter permissions affect query performance? Yes. Every query applies filter permissions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Filter permissions can affect query performance.
claims.quote: Does filter permissions affect query performance? Yes. Every query applies filter permissions. An efficient data model and filter design should mitigate performance problems.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Learn recommends efficient data modelling and filter design to mitigate filter-query performance problems.
claims.quote: An efficient data model and filter design should mitigate performance problems.

claims.claim: For filter queries involving a link-entity, Dataverse Search returns primary-table results only.
claims.quote: For filter queries that involve a link-entity relationship, such as Account linked to Contact, Dataverse Search returns results from the primary table only and doesn't include values from the linked table.

claims.claim: Deleting a Record Filter deletes its associated Entity Record Filters.
claims.quote: Deleting a record filter also deletes its associated entity record filters.

claims.claim: Filter permissions are not currently available for external virtual tables.
claims.quote: Can I use filter permissions to external virtual tables? Not currently.

claims.where: front matter: licensing model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The included licensing model uses the documented Power Apps or Power Automate entitlement for apps and flows using custom and Common Data Model Dataverse tables.
claims.quote: App makers can use most of the tables available within Microsoft Dataverse (including custom tables and tables that are part of the Common Data Model) to create apps and flows for users who have a Power Apps or Power Automate license.

claims.claim: App users need the corresponding Dynamics 365 application's licence to create, update or delete rows in its restricted tables.
claims.quote: tables that are tied to the functionality of Dynamics 365 apps (such as Dynamics 365 Sales or Dynamics 365 Customer Service) require app users to have the corresponding license for that application if they want to create, update, or delete rows within the tables.

claims.claim: Record filters can be created as solution components, supporting the advice to manage them through solutions.
claims.quote: An unmanaged solution and its unique name. All solution components created by the examples are associated with this solution.

claims.claim: Power Apps (maker) > environment > Solutions > solution > + New > More > Other > Record Filter reaches the form defining selected records.
claims.quote: Go to Power Apps. Select your environment. Go to Solutions and create a new solution or open an existing solution. Select + New. Select More and Other. Select Record Filter. ... Copy the FetchXML and paste it in the FetchXML box.
claims.fix: Extend controls[0].ui.path to 'environment > Solutions > solution > + New > More > Other > Record Filter > FetchXML'. The cited page identifies FetchXML as the deciding field on the form.

claims.claim: POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/recordfilters creates a filter using fetchxml, uniquename and displayname in its body.
claims.quote: POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/recordfilters HTTP/1.1 ... "displayname": "Stores in Redmond", "uniquename": "new_storesinredmond", "fetchxml": "<fetch>

claims.claim: Record Filter records can also be edited through PATCH.
claims.quote: Update Event: True | PATCH /recordfilters(recordfilterid) See Update

claims.claim: Power Apps (maker) > environment > Solutions > solution > + New > More > Other > EntityRecordFilter reaches the table-association form.
claims.quote: Return to your Solution. Select + New. Select More and Other. Select EntityRecordFilter. Enter a Name ... Select the Record Filter ... Enter the Related Entity, the logical name of the table, such as account.
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path to 'environment > Solutions > solution > + New > More > Other > EntityRecordFilter > Record Filter > Related Entity', following the cited form's filter selection and table field.

claims.claim: POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/entityrecordfilters attaches a filter using objecttypecode and the RecordFilterId navigation property.
claims.quote: POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/entityrecordfilters HTTP/1.1 ... { "name": "Stores in Redmond", "objecttypecode": "new_store", "RecordFilterId@odata.bind": "/recordfilters(00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001)" }

claims.claim: The admin-centre route is Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Security roles > security role > table > filter privilege.
claims.quote: Open a security role. Select the target table. Select the filter privilege. Grant the privilege to the role. Assign the role to users or teams.

claims.claim: POST [Organization Uri]/api/data/v9.2/roles(<roleid>)/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.AddPrivilegesRole adds role privileges through the Privileges collection.
claims.quote: Pass the list as the AddPrivilegesRole.Privileges parameter. ... POST [Organization Uri]/api/data/v9.2/roles(44ee44ee-ff55-aa66-bb77-88cc88cc88cc)/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.AddPrivilegesRole HTTP/1.1

claims.claim: The action's RolePrivilege entries can carry RecordFilterId to identify the privilege's Record Filter.
claims.quote: RecordFilterId | Edm.Guid | The Record Filter of the privilege. ... AddPrivilegesRole | Privileges Parameter

claims.claim: The System Administrator security role cannot be edited.
claims.quote: You can't edit the System Administrator security role.

claims.claim: Microsoft instructs administrators to copy the System Administrator role and change the copy instead.
claims.quote: Instead, copy the System Administrator security role and make changes to the new role.

claims.claim: Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Manage security roles > security role manages users' role assignments.
claims.quote: On the Users page select a user, and then select Manage security roles. Select or deselect security roles. ... The specified steps help you manage only direct role assignments for the user.
claims.fix: Append to controls[3].note: 'This UI manages direct role assignments only; roles inherited through group teams are managed separately.' This qualification is stated at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/assign-security-roles.

claims.claim: The printed v9.0 systemuserroles_association POST directly assigns the role whose URI is supplied in @odata.id.
claims.quote: POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.0/systemusers(azureactivedirectoryobjectid=<user object ID>)/systemuserroles_association/$ref ... { "@odata.id":"[Organization URI]/api/data/v9.0/roles(<role ID>)" }

claims.claim: Assigning security roles requires at least Read and Assign privileges on the Security Role table.
claims.quote: To assign security roles to a user, you need to have the appropriate privileges (minimum privileges are Read and Assign on the Security Role table).

claims.claim: An assigner cannot grant a security role with more privileges than they hold.
claims.quote: To prevent elevation of security role privileges, the person who is assigning the security role can't assign someone else to a security role that has more privileges than the assigner.

claims.claim: The filter-based security feature pages themselves describe granting filter privileges through the security role editor rather than publishing an automation example for that step.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Dataverse filter-based security filtered record ownership record filter privileges'. Read admin Grant filter privileges, maker Create and assign a security role, and developer Grant access with security roles; they give or link editor steps, not a privilege-grant API example.

claims.claim: Deleting a Record Filter removes access granted through its associated Entity Record Filters.
claims.quote: A security role then grants access to the filtered rows for one or more operations. ... Deleting a record filter also deletes its associated entity record filters. Before changing or removing a filter, review every role that grants it to avoid unintended changes in data access.

claims.claim: Filter-based security works with filtered, user/team and organisation record ownership tables.
claims.quote: You can use filter-based security with: Filtered record ownership tables. User or team record ownership tables. Organization record ownership tables.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout; rationale: risk
claims.claim: On organisation-owned tables, filter privileges add matching-record access without reducing broader security-role access.
claims.quote: Standard privileges for an organization record ownership table grant access to all records in the table. Filter privileges provide another way to grant access to matching records. They don't reduce broader access that a security role already grants.

claims.where: Governance controls; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Users receive filter privileges through assigned security roles and team memberships.
claims.quote: Users receive all filter privileges from their assigned security roles and team memberships.

claims.claim: Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Security roles reaches the role list in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Select Manage on the navigation pane. On the Manage pane, select Environments and then select an environment. On the command bar, select Settings. Expand Users + permissions and select Security roles. Choose the security role you want to edit.
